newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia's Alatas sees no quick Timor solution.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia's Alatas sees no quick Timor solution.

text.p: Indonesian Foreign Minister Ali Alatas said on Monday he saw no quick solution to the problem of the former Portuguese colony of East Timor.

"We don't know when the East Timor issue will be over. The problem of East Timor also depends on Portugal and the United Nations, which make it an issue," Alatas told a parliamentary commission dealing with foreign policy.
"So if Portugal is not ready yet to solve it, the effort to find a solution will go on and on," he said without elaborating.

Indonesia invaded the territory in 1975 and absorbed it as its 27th province the following year. The move has not been recognised by the United Nations, which still regards Portugal as the territory's administering power.

U.N.-sponsored meetings of the foreign ministers of both countries last month led to an agreement that senior officials of the two sides would hold more substantial talks on East Timor beginning on July 28.

The latest discussions between Alatas and Portuguese Foreign Minister Jaime Gama were the ninth in a series that began in 1983, and the first since U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan took office in January.
East Timor has recently been hit by its worst violence in years. Rebels resisting Jakarta's rule tried to disrupt Indonesia's May 29 general election with a series of attacks in East Timor.

At least 37 people have died in clashes since the eve of polling day, including 16 policemen and one soldier in a single ambush. Police have said that more than 70 people have been detained over the same period.
